what: Holding screen with countdown, today's match-ups and the sponsor panel. Music bed, then the show open.
detail: The first thing viewers see should already look like the event. AOBS builds the holding screen in the tournament's identity: countdown, match card, bracket stage and a sponsor slot that runs before a single game starts.
caption: Mini Mayhem, semi-final. Holding screen with countdown, match-ups and the Shadhin Host panel.

what: Pick/ban board, filled from the game client as each hero locks in.
detail: Bans, picks and the phase timer come from the draft itself, so the board is never behind the casters. Best-of series and round number sit on the board too.
caption: Pakistan Community Cup, grand final. Ban phase, best of 5, round 1.

what: Observers follow the fight. In-game HUD: score, gold, turrets, timer, minimap, both rosters.
detail: Observers read the map ahead of the action so the right fight is already on screen. The HUD frames it: team scoreboard, gold, turrets and the game clock across the top; minimap and both player rails at the sides.
caption: Pakistan Community Cup, grand final. AOBS in-game HUD.

what: Squeeze-back: the game keeps running inside an L-frame while the sponsor message runs around it.
detail: Sponsors get airtime without the audience losing the game. On Mini Mayhem the sponsor ran three ways: squeeze-back, an in-game ad slot and the holding-screen panel.
caption: Mini Mayhem, top eight. Squeeze-back for Shadhin Host; gameplay stays live.

what: Key plays clipped as they happen and rolled back at the next break, stinger in and out.
detail: Replay runs as its own position, so the director never has to choose between the live game and the moment everyone wants to see again.

what: Gold graph, team comparison and standings, built from match data.
detail: Numbers come straight from the match, so the panel is ready when the casters are. The same data feeds the bracket and standings graphics.

what: A second stream runs hot. If the primary drops, the backup takes programme and the channel stays up.
detail: Backup Streamer is our own failover system. It runs from the first frame to the last, so an encoder crash or a dropped line is a log entry, not an offline screen.

what: Programme encoded in AOBS Cloud and delivered to Twitch, YouTube and Kick.
detail: One programme, every platform. AOBS Cloud also lets the gallery run remotely, so an online event needs no venue build.
